 The One Player Kevin Cash Is Worried About for the World Series Opener
 Pardon Joshua 2026년 10월 23일 금 오후 9:10 UTC 0 Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash knows his hitters face a difficult assignment against Milwaukee Brewers right-hander Jacob Misiorowski in the opener this fall.
 Cash said avoiding pitches outside the strike zone is essential against the hard-throwing starter.
 “As soon as you start expanding out of the zone with a guy as special and talented as Misiorowski is, it really works in his favor,” Cash said, via Ryan Bass. “To have those lengthy at-bats, try to get the fastball down, that’s very much easier said than done because he’s got so much ride and carry through the zone.”
 Misiorowski averaged 100.6 mph on his fastball during the regular season. His velocity makes it difficult for hitters to square up pitches, increasing the importance of patience and selection.
 Misiorowski led the majors with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts. However, he has failed to complete five innings in either of his first two postseason starts.
 Advertisement
 That creates an opportunity for Tampa Bay if its hitters can make Misiorowski work. Foul balls and extended at-bats could increase his pitch count and force Milwaukee to turn to its bullpen earlier.
 Cash’s warning reflects the balance the Rays must find. They need to attack pitches in the zone while avoiding elevated fastballs and pitches outside the strike zone.
 Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash (16)Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Misiorowski will start Game 1 for Milwaukee, while Tampa Bay has selected Nick Martinez to oppose him. Martinez gives the Rays a veteran option as both franchises pursue their first World Series title.
 The opener begins Friday night at American Family Field. Cash’s message is clear: Tampa Bay must make Misiorowski earn every out rather than help him with impatient swings.
